task.prompt: Implement task_func(data=None). With no argument, load inputs/experiment.json; otherwise process the supplied data mapping. It contains candidate, controls (two method names) and rows, each with method, task_id, family and accepted. Each method has one row for every task. Return a report and write that same object to report.json on every call. Required keys: tasks (distinct task IDs), accepted (exact True counts by method), ungraded_programs (accepted values whose type is not bool), comparisons, families, superiority_supported, evidence="recorded_checked_program_outcomes". families maps each family to exact True counts by method. For each control, comparisons contains wins (candidate True/control False), losses (candidate False/control True), p_numerator and p_denominator as DECIMAL STRINGS, gain_numerator (candidate accepted minus control accepted), gain_denominator (tasks), passes_gain, passes_significance. For n=wins+losses use the exact one-sided binomial tail: numerator=sum(comb(n,k) for k from wins through n), denominator=2**n, without fraction reduction. passes_gain is 25*gain_numerator >= tasks, passes_significance is 80*numerator <= denominator. Overall superiority_supported requires at least98 tasks, zero ungraded programs, both comparison gates for both controls, and candidate accepted count no more than2 below either control in every family. Do not equate a numerical lead with a passed gate. The function must handle different real cohorts and different method names; it will also be checked on a separate actual recorded course.
